source.title: Text-to-CadQuery: A New Paradigm for CAD Generation with Scalable Large Model Capabilities

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream CAD-generation performance across model sizes, using task metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws and tests whether larger fine-tuned models perform better on CAD generation. It reports CAD task metrics across model sizes, not held-out cross-entropy, power-law fits, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocations. The Text2CAD baseline comparison concerns output format and is not a model-size result for the claim.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in a new setting: CAD-code generation after fine-tuning six pretrained LLMs from 124M to 7B. It reports task metrics by model size (Table 3, Figure 4). The sweep is uncontrolled: it spans different model families and configurations (CodeGPT/GPT-2, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral), and the 7B model alone uses 4-bit LoRA with different epochs and learning rate. It fits no scaling curve and does not relate performance to pretraining loss. T3 fits better than T2, since this is a new downstream setting rather than a different method on the original question.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors claim a clear, consistent scaling trend: larger fine-tuned models give more accurate and executable CadQuery. They concede that 7B underperforms 3B on accuracy, which they attribute to limited data, while 7B has the lowest Invalid Rate. The record's 'generally improve' is fairer than the authors' 'consistent', since Invalid Rate is non-monotone below 3B.
record.recipe_differences: Measures CAD-generation task metrics after supervised fine-tuning or LoRA across different pretrained models; does not reproduce pretraining-loss or compute-optimal scaling-law measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model family and size, training method (SFT versus LoRA), metric, and available task-training data; the authors suggest limited data constrains the 7B model.
record.problems: The comparison uses different model families and training configurations rather than a controlled size sweep within one model family. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported. Outcomes are task-specific CAD metrics, not pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: The Text2CAD Transformer baseline in Table 3 is omitted because it is an output-format comparator, not a pretrained model-size result relevant to V6.

untested.parts: Predictability (no fitted trend or extrapolation); downstream performance against pretraining loss; a controlled within-family size sweep; tasks other than text-to-CadQuery.
Not tested: no pretraining loss reported.
Not tested: no fits or extrapolation.
Not tested: no shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: no power-law fit of fine-tuning loss.
Not tested: no exponents are fitted.

missing.what: GPT-4.1 mini fine-tuned on a 10k subset: 0% Invalid Rate, with accuracy matching the 7B model. Used by the authors to argue that larger models execute more reliably but need data; size is undisclosed.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Kaplan et al. as motivation. The size sweep confounds parameter count with model family, pretraining corpus (CodeGPT is code-pretrained), epochs, learning rate, batch size and fine-tuning method (SFT vs 4-bit LoRA at 7B). No seeds or uncertainty are reported. Most F1/IoU rows are figure-only, with states inferred from the authors' text.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameters, tokens, or compute measurement.
No small-run power-law fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute-budget comparison or parameter/token allocation sweep.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns fine-tuned CAD generation, but does not measure whether a power-law loss form holds in fine-tuning or another training regime.
Tests CAD-generation task metrics across model sizes after fine-tuning; does not test other downstream tasks or downstream performance against pretraining loss.
No loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across setup choices.

relationships.condition: Accuracy metrics (CD, Gemini evaluation, F1, IoU), models from 124M to 3B across mixed families
relationships.reason: CD median falls 0.234→0.191 and Gemini accuracy rises 60.28%→69.30% roughly monotonically; the text says F1 and IoU improve steadily up to 3B (r05,r06,r09,r10,r12-r14,r16-r18,r20,r29-r44).
relationships.display_finding: Median CD decreased from 0.234 to 0.191 and Gemini accuracy increased from 60.28% to 69.30% roughly monotonically, while F1 and IoU improved steadily up to 3B.

relationships.reason: Invalid Rate is non-monotone (9.4, 15.6, 13.8, 8.4, 6.5, 1.32), and GPT-2 medium shows no Gemini gain over CodeGPT-small; pretraining data (code vs general) matters more than size at small scale (r07,r08,r11,r15,r19,r23).
relationships.display_finding: Invalid Rate varied nonmonotonically through 9.4, 15.6, 13.8, 8.4, 6.5 and 1.32, while GPT-2 medium showed no Gemini evaluation gain over CodeGPT-small.

relationships.reason: Accuracy at 7B falls below 3B on CD, Gemini evaluation, F1 and IoU, which the authors attribute to limited fine-tuning data. This is confounded by LoRA and a different family, so it qualifies the trend rather than refuting it (r21,r22,r24,r45-r48).
relationships.display_finding: The 7B model underperformed 3B on CD, Gemini evaluation, F1 and IoU, which the authors attributed to limited fine-tuning data, with model-family and LoRA differences also present.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuned models from 124M through 3B on Text-to-CadQuery, for geometric accuracy metrics
reader_labels.reason: Chamfer Distance and Gemini evaluation improve through Qwen2.5-3B, and the text describes improving F1 and IoU through 3B (rows r01-r02, r04-r06, r08-r10, r12-r14, r16-r18, r20, r25-r44).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The 7B Mistral model and metric-specific outcomes
reader_labels.reason: Mistral-7B has worse Chamfer Distance and Gemini evaluation than Qwen2.5-3B and does not further improve the plotted F1 or IoU metrics, while its Invalid Rate is best; thus performance does not rise uniformly with size across metrics (rows r21-r24, r45-r48).
